Cosmetic.headline: Bonding or veneers? Know the difference.
Cosmetic.primary:
Before anyone touches your teeth, you should know this.

Composite bonding is added to your tooth. It usually needs little or no preparation, it's often done in a single visit, and if it ever chips it can be repaired.

Veneers involve preparing the front of the tooth first. That can't be reversed. They're the right answer for some smiles, but it's a decision you make once.

Most people looking online don't know the difference. They pick a price or a photo, and find out what was involved afterwards.

At your consultation we look at your teeth and tell you which option would actually help, including when the answer is the smaller one. You get a written plan with the price for each option before anything starts.

Cosmetic.headline: Bonding: the honest answers.
Cosmetic.primary:
Will composite bonding stain? Yes, it can.

You've probably read that on a forum already, along with "it chips" and "it won't last". Some of that's fair, so here's the straight version.

Tea, coffee and tobacco can stain bonding over time. A cosmetic polish helps keep it looking fresh, and regular hygiene visits help too. If a bit chips, it can be repaired, rather than started again. And you can help it along by not using your teeth to open things.

Why do people choose it anyway? Because it's added to your own teeth with little or no preparation, it's often done in a single visit, and you keep the teeth underneath. Veneers involve preparing the tooth, which can't be reversed.

At your consultation we'll tell you which suits your teeth and your habits, and give you a written plan with the price before anything starts. Composite bonding from £300.
